title: Shockwave
subtitle: Build a readable shockwave with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: An impact creates a threat that travels across a surface.
overview: An impact creates a threat that travels across a surface, separating the boss’s strike location from the later line the player must clear.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a shockwave as one rule.

demo.title: Test the shockwave
phaseDescriptions: Emphasize the source impact and the surface that will carry the wave; height and travel direction should be visible at release.
The player jumps, changes elevation, blocks, moves beyond the wave’s reach, or exploits a deliberate break in the surface.
The wave must pass the player’s complete body before it dissipates, while the impact pose holds a short recovery that rewards a correctly timed crossing.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Emphasize the source impact and the surface that will carry the wave; height and travel direction should be visible at release.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player jumps, changes elevation, blocks, moves beyond the wave’s reach, or exploits a deliberate break in the surface.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The wave must pass the player’s complete body before it dissipates, while the impact pose holds a short recovery that rewards a correctly timed crossing.

mistakes.title: A wave hidden by floor art or camera effects becomes a reaction test to an unreadable hazard
mistakes.body: A wave hidden by floor art or camera effects becomes a reaction test to an unreadable hazard.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible shockwave cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune travel speed, height, lifetime, surface coverage, and repeated spacing against jump airtime and landing control.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Alternate low and high waves, split them at obstacles, or repeat them in a learnable rhythm after the base traversal is clear.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The wave must pass the player’s complete body before it dissipates, while the impact pose holds a short recovery that rewards a correctly timed crossing.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: An impact creates a threat that travels across a surface, separating the boss’s strike location from the later line the player must clear. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player jumps, changes elevation, blocks, moves beyond the wave’s reach, or exploits a deliberate break in the surface. Tune travel speed, height, lifetime, surface coverage, and repeated spacing against jump airtime and landing control.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: A wave hidden by floor art or camera effects becomes a reaction test to an unreadable hazard. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
At least one route remains reachable with the movement options available at this point.

examples.game: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
examples.body: Horn Beetle demonstrates shockwave in a 2D encounter. Emphasize the source impact and the surface that will carry the wave; height and travel direction should be visible at release.
False Knight demonstrates shockwave in a 2D encounter. The player jumps, changes elevation, blocks, moves beyond the wave’s reach, or exploits a deliberate break in the surface.
Godfrey, First Elden Lord demonstrates shockwave in a 3D encounter. Tune travel speed, height, lifetime, surface coverage, and repeated spacing against jump airtime and landing control.
